t: You're on Little Portland Street, in the City of Westminster. The street takes its name from William Cavendish-Bentinck, the third Duke of Portland. He was a Whig and then a Tory politician, and he was prime minister twice, in 1783 and again from 1807 until 1809. That gap of twenty-three years between his two terms is the longest of any British prime minister. So the name on the street sign is that of a very unusual premier.
